correctness.rationale: For every real circular BV derivative the zero-mass Jordan decomposition and a positive coupling reduce the sharp quotient to one half the maximal L1 kernel-translate distance, with attainment by indicators of arcs. An exact harmonic factorization yields the all-separation piecewise expression (2). Exact differentiation and factorization show the unique global critical point z_+=(2+sqrt(2))/8; substitution gives the stated radical. The critical first-published hypotheses (real signed measure, circular endpoint variation, 2pi normalization, all separations, singular derivative jumps and attained sharpness) are covered. Exact-Q(sqrt(2)) algebra and independent sign-split antiderivative checks replay from checks/check_bv_fourier2.py; finite random tests only corroborate the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: A new exact real-BV operator norm for the continuous five-mode projector with a unique nonantipodal maximizing arc separation, √(71+8√2)/(2π), was checked against the published low-frequency total-variation reconstruction results and the closest accessible projection-norm records by implication. The existing zero-mass kernel-distance technique is recognized as standard; none of these inspected statements evaluates the same sign-changing degree-two Dirichlet-kernel separation functional. Residual risk: an older specialized identity in unindexed approximation literature could coincide.
residual_risks: Standard Dobrushin/zero-mass convolution duality is pre-existing; an unindexed classical evaluation for degree two could already contain the same radical and optimizing arc separation.
The checked finite-group and reconstruction references do not exhaust older trigonometric approximation literature; no independently verified historical priority claim is made.
All inputs and all operator bounds are real; complex measures are a different norm geometry.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial two-harmonic low-pass Fourier cutoff is a canonical stability benchmark for gradient-sparse periodic signals: its kernel difference can change sign internally, unlike a single harmonic. The exact BV norm and the surprising uniquely nonantipodal worst-case jump separation resolve the natural five-mode case completely, determining both a sharp operator invariant and the precise worst-conditioned arc geometry. This is not a selected arbitrary parameter slice or a mere normalizing check; it provides a sharp baseline for stable variation estimates of low-pass approximations. No extrapolation to other cutoffs is needed for this concrete value.
